text: Twenty-one videos of real work — the intake, the SQL, the dashboard, the Python check, the Tableau rebuild, the Excel reconciliation, two bug fixes, a finance reconciliation — all get compressed into the one document that actually gets read: a single page.

A one-page summary succeeds on what gets left out. Every fact that doesn't change the Sales Director's next decision, including most of the troubleshooting that was essential to get here, is a candidate for deletion.

The order that actually works: the headline finding first, the specific root cause second, the dollar impact third, the recommendation fourth, and one line acknowledging finance's different number — because that's the order a reader's own questions arrive in.

The DAX double-counting fix and the Python boundary bug mattered enormously to getting a trustworthy number, but neither one changes what she should decide next, so neither one makes it onto this page.
Every number on the page still has to be traceable. A short appendix keeps the backup, so if she asks where 1,580 or $540,000 came from, the answer is immediate, not 'let me go check.'

The real test: could someone who sat through none of the last twenty-one videos understand exactly what happened and what to do next, from this page alone, in under a minute? If yes, the whole series has done its job.
